nodes.name: Hydrothermal Ni(OH)2 formation
nodes.procedure: A precursor solution containing Ni(NO3)·6H2O, NH4F, and urea was prepared to facilitate the in situ formation of Ni(OH)2 nanosheets on NF (nickel foam).
nodes.source_text: The Pt@Ni2Pv/NF catalyst was fabricated via a four-step process comprising hydrothermal treatment... a precursor solution containing Ni(NO3)·6H2O, NH4F, and urea was prepared to facilitate the in situ formation of Ni(OH)2 nanosheets on NF

nodes.name: Phosphorization
nodes.procedure: Subsequent phosphating treatment yielded Ni2P/NF while preserving the nanosheet structure.
nodes.source_text: Subsequent phosphating treatment yielded Ni2P/NF while preserving the nanosheet structure (Figure S4, Supporting Information). High-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) images confirmed the nanosheet structure as Ni2P, with an interplanar spacing of 0.22 nm corresponding to the (111) plane.

nodes.description: HER LSV comparison of all catalysts in 1 M KOH + seawater (pH 14)
nodes.source_text: To assess the alkaline electrocatalytic performance, all samples were tested in 1 M KOH + seawater electrolyte (pH 14) using a standard three-electrode configuration... LSV curves reveal that Pt@Ni₂P_v/NF delivers superior HER performance... current densities of 100, 500, and 1000 mA cm⁻² at... 37.2, 68.8, and 89.0 mV... Tafel slope... 23.24 mV dec⁻¹... Faradaic efficiency... 96.3%

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images of Pt@Ni₂Pᵥ/NF show nanoparticles along the roughened edges of the nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 1a, nanoparticles appeared along the roughened edges of the nanosheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice spacing of 0.24 nm corresponding to the (111) planes of Ni₂P, indicating lattice contraction induced by Pt NCs doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The observed lattice spacings of 0.24 nm (Figure 1b) corresponded to the (111) planes of Ni₂P, indicating lattice contraction induced by Pt NCs doping.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM visualizes atomic clusters of Pt with larger clusters marked by yellow dashed circles and smaller ones by red.
nodes.evidence_snippet: in Figure 1c, aberration-corrected high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADFSTEM) visualized atomic clusters of Pt...

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED patterns of Pt@Ni₂Pᵥ confirm distinct diffraction rings corresponding to the (111) planes of Ni₂P.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SAED patterns (Figure 1d) of Pt@Ni₂Pᵥ confirmed distinct diffraction rings corresponding to the (111) planes of Ni₂P.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mappings and line-scan analysis demonstrate uniform distribution of Pt, Ni, and P throughout the Pt@Ni₂Pᵥ nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EDS elemental mappings analysis (Figure 1e) and TEM-EDS line-scan analysis (Figure S12, Supporting Information) further demonstrated the uniform distribution of Pt, Ni, and P...

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES shows Pt loading in Pt@Ni₂Pᵥ is 1.74 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES) was conducted... the Pt loading in Pt@Ni₂Pᵥ is 1.74 wt.%.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns of Pt@Ni₂Pᵥ powder match well with the Ni₂P crystal phase (PDF No. 03-0953) with weaker reflections of Ni(PO₃)₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The observed diffraction peaks match well with the Ni₂P crystal phase (PDF No. 03-0953). Additionally, several weaker reflections correspond to Ni(PO₃)₂ crystal phase...

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR shows Ni₂Pᵥ displays strong signal at g = 2.004 indicating higher density of unpaired electrons confirming P vacancies; Pt@Ni₂Pᵥ shows slightly decreased intensity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ni₂Pᵥ displays a strong signal at g = 2.004, in contrast to the much weaker response from Ni₂P... In Pt@Ni₂Pᵥ, the intensity of the EPR signal... slightly decreases...

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Ni 2p peaks shift negatively in Ni₂Pᵥ (P 2p at 132.09 eV) indicating electron transfer from Pᵥ to neighboring Ni and P atoms; Pt@Ni₂Pᵥ shows positive shift and Pt 4f peaks at 68.15, 72.73, 76.03 eV corresponding to Pt⁰.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the binding energies of Ni and P (e.g., P at 132.09 eV) in Ni₂Pᵥ exhibit a negative shift compared to Ni₂P, indicating electron transfer from Pᵥ to neighboring Ni and P atoms... The XPS spectrum of Pt... presents three peaks at 68.15, 72.73, and 76.03 eV corresponding to Pt⁰...

nodes.characterization_summary: UPS shows VBM of Ni₂P elevated by 1.13 eV vs Pt@Ni₂Pᵥ and 0.21 eV vs Ni₂Pᵥ; work function (WF) of Pt@Ni₂Pᵥ is 4.56 eV (lower than Ni₂Pᵥ 5.30 eV and Ni₂P 5.53 eV), indicating enhanced electron transfer capability.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the VBM of Ni₂P is elevated by 1.13 and 0.21 eV compared to Pt@Ni₂Pᵥ and Ni₂Pᵥ, respectively... The WF of Pt@Ni₂Pᵥ is determined to be 4.56 eV, which is lower than those of Ni₂Pᵥ (5.30 eV) and Ni₂P (5.53 eV)...

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt@Ni₂Pᵥ/NF exhibits superhydrophilic behavior with water contact angle approaching zero vs bare NF ≈90°.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the Pt@Ni₂Pᵥ/NF electrode exhibits superhydrophilic, with a water contact angle (WCA) approaching zero, whereas bare NF has a WCA of ≈90°...
